newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - GOV'T OUTLINES ENERGY DEBT SCHEDULE.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - GOV'T OUTLINES ENERGY DEBT SCHEDULE.

text.p: The Lithuanian government on Friday outlined its debt schedule to the state-run Lithuanian Energy (LE) company, to which it owes 776 million litas.
The government's press office said in a statement that the complicated debt situation, which goes both ways, had been untangled.

Under the scheme, the government said it was assuming responsibility for a number of LE's debts and cancelling the sum it owes to the state budget, reducing its direct debt to LE by 639 million litas to 136.8 million litas.
The government said that it would pay the 136.8 million litas by December 31, 1999.
The statement said that the debt might be financed by issuing state Treasury bills and through funds borrowed internally and internationally.
The government added that LE owed it 226.3 million litas for International Monetary Fund (IMF) credits.
It said that the state would assume responsibility for LE's debt of 159 million litas to Vilniaus Bank, Hermis Bank and the Lithuanian Savings Bank.
The statement also said that the finance ministry had agreed to cancel the 72.2 million litas Lithuanian Energy owes to the budget and the 181 million litas owed by the Ignalina nulcear power plant.
